desc: Implement the solution using Fenwick Trees (BIT). Specifically:
Initialize two BITs for set $V$ (positions and values) and two BITs for set $U$ (positions and values).
Compute the initial inversion count for $k=0$ by querying the $V$ BITs (since $U$ is empty) and store/print it.
Populate the $V$ BITs with all elements initially.
Identify elements $p$ that wrap at this step (where $A_p = M - 1 - k$).
Calculate the change in inversion count based on the derived logic (interactions with remaining $V$ and existing $U$).
